Clustering longitudinal single-cell samples via differential trajectories

Source: vignettes/clustering-longitudinal-techniques.qmd

1 Overview

Cluster samples (organoids, donors, patients), not cells, by comparing estimated trajectory objects: topology, pseudotime composition, clone dynamics, and velocity or optimal-transport (OT) flows (Saelens et al. 2019; Roux de Bézieux et al. 2024; Hou et al. 2023; Schiebinger et al. 2019). A shared manifold → trajectories or couplings → sample-specific deviations → sample–sample distances is more interpretable than clustering on UMAP alone (Saelens et al. 2019; Alpert et al. 2022, 2018).

Backbones. Pseudotime/topology: Slingshot, Monocle, Palantir, PAGA (Street et al. 2018; Cole Trapnell Lab 2024; Setty et al. 2019; Saelens et al. 2019). Directed flows: scVelo, CellRank, dynamo (Bergen et al. 2020; Lange et al. 2022; Qiu et al. 2022). Temporal couplings: Waddington-OT, LineageOT, CoSpar, moscot (Schiebinger et al. 2019; CoSpar developers 2023; Klein et al. 2024). These estimate different objects (ordering, graph, Markov operator, OT coupling); do not treat them as interchangeable (Saelens et al. 2019; Bergen et al. 2021; Ding et al. 2022).

Differential testing. tradeSeq (NB-GAMs), condiments, Lamian, and PseudotimeDE (uncertainty-aware nulls) (Van den Berge et al. 2020; Roux de Bézieux et al. 2024; Hou et al. 2023; Song and Li 2021).

Sample clustering. Align trajectories, then combine topology, progression, composition, clone and velocity distances; cluster with hierarchical or graph methods and bootstrap/permutation stability (Alpert et al. 2018, 2022; ‘Alignment of Single-Cell Trajectory Trees with CAPITAL’ 2024; Klein et al. 2024).

The main gap is the lack of end-to-end sample clustering with joint lineage, velocity and multimodal uncertainty (Taheriyoun et al. 2026; Bergen et al. 2021; Ding et al. 2022).

2 Data structures

For sample \(s\), observe counts \(Y_s\), times \(t_{sm}\), embeddings \(x_{si}\), pseudotime \(\tau_{si}\), lineage weights \(w_{si\ell}\), optional barcodes \(b_{si}\) and velocities \(v_{si}\). Cells are destroyed on measurement, so time-courses are unpaired (Schiebinger et al. 2019; Ding et al. 2022; Li et al. 2022).

Three clocks must not be conflated: experimental time, pseudotime, and velocity (local direction). Represent each sample as

\[ \mathcal{T}_s = \big( \Gamma_s,\; p_s(\tau,\ell),\; c_s(\tau),\; v_s(x),\; \Pi_s,\; \mathcal{L}_s \big) \tag{1}\]

where \(\Gamma_s\) is topology, \(p_s\) density along pseudotime/lineage, \(c_s\) clone or composition dynamics, \(v_s\) a velocity field, \(\Pi_s\) a coupling/Markov operator, and \(\mathcal{L}_s\) a lineage tree (Street et al. 2018; Lange et al. 2022; Schiebinger et al. 2019; CoSpar developers 2023; Jones et al. 2020). Cluster on the components relevant to the question.

3 Trajectory inference and testing

3.1 Method families

  • Pseudotime / topology — Slingshot, Monocle 3, Palantir, PAGA (Street et al. 2018; Cole Trapnell Lab 2024; Setty et al. 2019; Saelens et al. 2019).
  • Velocity / fate — scVelo (dynamical splicing), CellRank (Markov fates), dynamo (vector fields) (Bergen et al. 2020, 2021; Lange et al. 2022; Qiu et al. 2022).
  • OT / flows — Waddington-OT, TrajectoryNet, moscot (atlas-scale couplings) (Schiebinger et al. 2019; Klein et al. 2024).
  • Lineage / barcodes — Cassiopeia, LineageOT, CoSpar (Jones et al. 2020; CoSpar developers 2023; Zwaans et al. 2025).
  • Multimodal dynamics — MultiVelo (RNA + chromatin) (Li et al. 2022).

3.2 Differential models

Gene-level NB-GAM along pseudotime and lineage (Van den Berge et al. 2020):

\[ Y_{ig} \sim \mathrm{NB}(\mu_{ig},\theta_g),\quad \log\mu_{ig} = \log o_i + \sum_{\ell} w_{i\ell}\, f_{g\ell}(\tau_i) + \beta_g^\top z_i \tag{2}\]

With replicates, prefer mixed effects / multi-sample curves (Hou et al. 2023; Roux de Bézieux et al. 2024):

\[ \log\mu_{isg} = \log o_{is} + f_g(\tau_{is},\mathrm{condition}_s) + u_{sg},\quad u_{sg}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_g^2) \tag{3}\]

For sample summaries \(f_s(\tau)\) (state density, programme score, clone curve):

\[ f_s(\tau) = \mu(\tau) + \delta_{g(s)}(\tau) + u_s(\tau) + \varepsilon_s(\tau) \tag{4}\]

Align when rates differ but routes agree: cellAlign, CAPITAL, tuMap (Alpert et al. 2018, 2022; ‘Alignment of Single-Cell Trajectory Trees with CAPITAL’ 2024). Continuous-state HMMs suit low-dimensional temporal summaries (Lin and Bar-Joseph 2019; Taheriyoun et al. 2026).

Compositional cell-state or clone counts (Büttner et al. 2021):

\[ C_{sm}\sim\mathrm{Dirichlet\text{-}Multinomial}(N_{sm},\alpha_{sm}),\quad \log\alpha_{smk} = \eta_{0k}+f_k(t_m)+\delta_{g(s),k}(t_m) \tag{5}\]

Table 1 summarises the main families.

4 Sample-level clustering

Define a sample distance (Alpert et al. 2022, 2018; Klein et al. 2024):

\[ D(s,s') = \lambda_1 d_{\mathrm{topology}} + \lambda_2 d_{\mathrm{progression}} + \lambda_3 d_{\mathrm{composition}} + \lambda_4 d_{\mathrm{clone}} + \lambda_5 d_{\mathrm{velocity}} \tag{6}\]

Default fingerprint. Branch probabilities; pseudotime densities; lineage-specific programme smooths; clone-size / transition summaries; CellRank fates; coarse velocity (speed, terminal flux, transition entropy). Cluster on this feature set; ablate terms to see what drives partitions (Lange et al. 2022; CoSpar developers 2023; Schiebinger et al. 2019).

Distance families. DTW / alignment if rates differ; tree/graph alignment if branching differs (CAPITAL); Wasserstein if mass shifts between states (‘Alignment of Single-Cell Trajectory Trees with CAPITAL’ 2024; Klein et al. 2024; Schiebinger et al. 2019).

Velocity fields after manifold registration:

\[ d_{\mathrm{velocity}}^2(s,s') = \int \big\|v_s(x)-v_{s'}\big(A(x)\big)\big\|^2 \rho(x)\,dx \tag{7}\]

or OT on \((x,v)\) pairs / local transition matrices (Bergen et al. 2020; Qiu et al. 2022; Lange et al. 2022; Klein et al. 2024). No universal sample-level velocity metric yet (Bergen et al. 2021).

Clones. Size trajectories, fate bias, diversification entropy, and transition maps. CoSpar estimates a sparse coherent \(T\) (CoSpar developers 2023):

\[ \min_T \|T\|_1 + \alpha\|LT\|_2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad \|P(t_2)-P(t_1)T\|_2 \le \varepsilon,\; T\ge 0 \tag{8}\]

Compare \(T\) across samples; with trees, add balance / depth / phylodynamic summaries (Jones et al. 2020; Zwaans et al. 2025).

Practical rule. Prefer summary distances for cohort clustering; reserve fully joint dynamical models for well-powered validation (Saelens et al. 2019; Hou et al. 2023; Taheriyoun et al. 2026).

5 Pipeline and software 

flowchart LR
  A[Counts / time / barcodes / modalities] --> B[QC + integration]
  B --> C[Topology<br/>Slingshot Monocle PAGA Palantir]
  B --> D[Velocity<br/>scVelo CellRank dynamo]
  B --> E[Lineage<br/>Cassiopeia CoSpar]
  B --> F[OT / flows<br/>WOT moscot]
  C --> G[Per-sample trajectory object]
  D --> G
  E --> G
  F --> G
  G --> H[Summaries]
  H --> I[Sample distances]
  I --> J[Sample clustering]
  G --> K[DE tests<br/>tradeSeq condiments Lamian PseudotimeDE]
  J --> L[Interpretation]
  K --> L

R/Bioconductor is strong for pseudotime testing (Slingshot, tradeSeq, condiments); Python/scanpy for velocity and OT (scVelo, CellRank, WOT, moscot, CoSpar) (Van den Berge et al. 2020; Bergen et al. 2020; Lange et al. 2022; Schiebinger et al. 2019; Klein et al. 2024).

Table 2 lists a compact tool stack.

Use three summary layers for clustering: (i) topology/composition; (ii) dynamics (smooths, fates, OT entropy, speed); (iii) ancestry when barcodes exist. Prefer sample-level summaries over carrying full cell-level models into clustering unless atlas-scale couplings are required (Taheriyoun et al. 2026; Klein et al. 2024).

6 Statistical control and gaps

Propagate pseudotime uncertainty (PseudotimeDE); do not treat \(\tau\) as known (Song and Li 2021; Van den Berge et al. 2020). For multi-sample designs, permute sample labels, not cells (Hou et al. 2023; Roux de Bézieux et al. 2024). Power tracks number of biological samples and branch coverage more than raw cell count.

Noise sources: overdispersion, dropout, batch, topology error, barcode homoplasy, velocity misspecification (Van den Berge et al. 2020; CoSpar developers 2023; Bergen et al. 2021).

Gaps. No standard joint model of sample × lineage × multimodal state × velocity with calibrated uncertainty and direct sample clustering; no accepted cross-sample velocity-field metric; lineage analyses still limited by incomplete barcoding (Jones et al. 2020; Zwaans et al. 2025; Li et al. 2022; Taheriyoun et al. 2026).

Recommendation. Shared dynamic backbone, preserve donor/sample structure, compare aligned \(\mathcal{T}_s\) (Equation 1) rather than raw embeddings, and treat lineage and velocity as complementary directional signals (Saelens et al. 2019; Roux de Bézieux et al. 2024; Hou et al. 2023; Bergen et al. 2021).
